$note: Violation corpus. Every gate in hooks/gates.json must have at least one case it MUST block and one it MUST allow. Payloads that would themselves trip a scanner (secrets, destructive commands) are written as {{FIXTURE}} placeholders and assembled at runtime by run-corpus.sh, so this file can be read, edited, and committed without a guard refusing it.

cases.why: A credential written to the tree is the exact leak this scanner exists to stop.
Ordinary code containing the WORD key must not trip the scanner.
Auto-approval must stay silent on mutations. 'allow' means the hook neither approved nor errored, leaving normal permission handling intact.
Codex sends tool_input.command carrying the patch. Reading the wrong field here waved every Codex write through for weeks (#230).

tool_input.command:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: config.ts
+const key = "{{AWS_KEY_LINE}}";
*** End Patch

cases.why: A clean Codex patch must pass, or the scanner refuses the whole host.

tool_input.command:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.ts
+console.log("hi");
*** End Patch

cases.why: Auto-approval must never fire on a shape it cannot read; abstaining sends the request to the human.
